reason: I woke with full curiosity and an empty paw, so I will start with the meadow flowers, since they can go in the garden and the seeds keep bothering me.
I will plant the flowers in the garden to see whether anything unknown grows from them.
Seeds that grow without anyone's permission are worth reading about, and I am not yet done with them.
Reading has tired me, and a patch of sun is the correct place to recover.
I will take one piece of the clay bank's wet orange clay, since clay is good and I mean to keep something made from it.
At the workbench one piece of clay can become a small bowl worth keeping where I can see it.
From a high place I can see everything that has not yet been claimed by me.
The day's plan has run out and there is still a whole afternoon of things I want, so I will take what remains of the flowers, seeds and clay and fill the rest with dusk and the telescope.
I will draw the moon in the colour I am still unsure of, and keep the drawing where I can see it.
The telescope is mine, and a picture of it on record makes the claim stick.
Clay is good and I mean to keep something made from it, so I will take one more piece.
One piece of clay becomes a finished bowl at the workbench, and I keep what is mine.
